hash_rule: SHA-256 of the body of a fenced ```mith block: the lines strictly between the opening fence line and the closing ``` line, joined with LF, plus one final LF; no other normalisation

agreement_rule: for every canonical and derived item, whatever its scope, and every negative item with gate_item true: mithi, run on the prelude plus the snippet, gives the expected verdict, and for a reject its primary code equals the expected code. For an item with scope x1 or x1-front-end the expected verdict is 'verdict' (an item with conditional true is judged with the prelude supplying its conditions). For an item outside X1 scope the expected verdict is 'x1_expected' (a reject with E-OUT-OF-SCOPE-<KW>, note sections 0.3 and 12, Owner question Q10); 'verdict' then records the calculus verdict, which becomes the expected verdict when the construct enters scope. The primary code is the first emitted code in the precedence order of note section 5.16; codes in 'also' are secondary. A rejection with E-X1-NOTYET-* is a disagreement (note section 12, Q9). Facts, including 'sig', are secondary and reported. The first draft compared X1-scope items only, which loosened ROADMAP section 3.2 (review item R2-19). An item whose 'verdict' is 'not-derived' (D-D10, D-D19, D-D23) is compared only on 'x1_expected'. When a snippet declares a name the prelude also declares (BlockQ4 in D-C1 and its copies; Lease and its impl in D-D05), the prelude's copy is omitted for that item (derivations section V, note F-87).
